title: MongoDB wire protocol (OP_MSG)
summary: MongoDB's wire protocol (since MongoDB 3.6) uses OP_MSG as the primary message type. An OP_MSG: header (standard message header: length, requestID, responseTo, opCode=2013), then flags (4 bytes), then sections. Sections: type 0 (body, a single BSON document) or type 1 (document sequence, with identifier + documents). Checksum (optional, 4 bytes CRC32C) follows.

structure.meaning: Request ID being responded to (0 for requests).
Bit 0 = checksumPresent, bit 1 = moreToCome, bit 16 = exhaustAllowed.
0 = body (single BSON document), 1 = document sequence (identifier + count + documents).
A single BSON document containing the command and its arguments.
CRC32C of the message (if checksumPresent flag set).

ext.example_decoded: OP_MSG header: length 77, requestID 1, responseTo 0, opCode 2013 (OP_MSG)
notes: OP_MSG replaced the older OP_QUERY, OP_INSERT, OP_UPDATE, OP_DELETE, OP_GET_MORE, OP_KILL_CURSORS.
The body is a BSON document; the first key is the command name (e.g. 'find', 'insert', 'aggregate').
Document sequences (type 1) are used for bulk inserts.
MongoDB uses BSON (Binary JSON) for document storage and wire protocol.
